title: Aromatic Ethiopian Teff Muffins
description: These muffins are a delicious and diabetic-friendly Ethiopian dish featuring teff flour and a shio-koji cure, perfect for a cozy breakfast or snack, cooked to perfection on a comal.

ingredients.name: teff flour
ingredients.notes: make sure to use brown or ivory teff flour

ingredients.name: shio-koji
ingredients.notes: use a homemade or store-bought shio-koji cure

ingredients.name: milk
ingredients.notes: use a non-dairy milk alternative if desired

ingredients.name: honey
ingredients.notes: use a pure and raw honey

ingredients.name: baking powder
ingredients.notes: make sure to use a gluten-free baking powder

ingredients.name: ghee or oil
ingredients.notes: use a neutral-tasting oil or ghee

instructions: Preheat the comal or a non-stick skillet over medium heat.
Whisk together the teff flour, shio-koji, baking powder, and salt in a large bowl.
In a separate bowl, whisk together the eggs, milk, and honey until well combined.
Add the wet ingredients to the dry ingredients and stir until just combined, being careful not to overmix.
Add the ghee or oil and stir until the batter is smooth and free of lumps.
Using a 1/4 cup measuring cup, scoop the batter onto the preheated comal or skillet.
Cook the muffins for 3-4 minutes on the first side, or until the edges start to set and the surface is dry.
Flip the muffins and cook for an additional 2-3 minutes, or until golden brown and cooked through.
Remove the muffins from the comal or skillet and let cool on a wire rack for 5 minutes before serving.
